item_verdicts.call_sites: _find_compute_location is called only by resolve_location (locations.py:89). resolve_location is exported and @cache-decorated; callers reach it through resolve_service_url, get_port_offset and is_location_local in the same module. get_facility's unknown-facility path is ValueError (facility.py:139); _load_yaml returns an empty dict for a missing file (facility.py:64) so a facility with no config does not raise, preserving the fallback for unknown names without widening the catch. The other three 'except Exception' handlers in locations.py (_get_ssh_host at line ~168, get_port_offset at ~191, is_location_local at ~209) are outside the plan's named three and were left untouched, correctly, since the plan enumerates exactly the facility import plus the two config reads.
item_verdicts.diff: read against fd63244ce. In resolve_location the bare 'except Exception: pass' becomes 'except ValueError: pass' plus 'except Exception as exc: exc.add_note(...); raise'. In _find_compute_location the facility 'except Exception: return None' becomes 'except ImportError as exc: exc.add_note(...); raise' and the per-facility 'except Exception: continue' becomes 'except ValueError: continue' plus a re-raising 'except Exception as exc'. The test file adds a builtins.__import__ patch utility and four test functions (five cases once the resolver parametrization expands), pinning import propagation through both resolvers, the unknown-facility fallback, and config-read propagation through both the compute-locations search and the direct-location path.
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan's done-when has three parts. An injected ImportError at the facility import propagates out of both resolve_location and _find_compute_location: pinned by the parametrized test_facility_import_error_propagates[_find_compute_location|resolve_location] (tests/remote/test_locations_resolution.py:174-192), which patches builtins.__import__ to raise for imas_codex.discovery.base.facility and asserts __notes__ contains "while resolving location 'titan'". An unknown facility still yields the documented fallback: test_unknown_facility_keeps_direct_location_fallback asserts resolve_location('missing-facility-for-location-test') returns scheduler 'none', ssh_host equal to the location, is_compute False. The fragment gives the base and head counts and names the cause of each added failure: docs/evidence/fragments/discovery-judgments-through-jev/location-resolver-fail-closed.html. I reproduced all three behaviours independently (see evidence).
item_verdicts.goal: plan section 20's location-resolver-fail-closed node narrows the three swallowing handlers in imas_codex/remote/locations.py so an import or config-read failure propagates while an unknown facility keeps its fallback. All three named handlers are narrowed: the facility import in _find_compute_location (locations.py:127-131) now catches ImportError, adds a note and re-raises; the per-facility read in _find_compute_location (locations.py:134-140) catches ValueError and continues, re-raising any other exception with a note; and the get_facility read in resolve_location (locations.py:99-112) catches ValueError and passes, re-raising any other exception with a note. ValueError is the exception get_facility actually raises for an unknown facility (imas_codex/discovery/base/facility.py:139-140, 'Unknown facility: {facility_id}'), so the fallback condition matches the plan's requirement.

justifications.durability: the guards fire and I showed them doing it: the base arm fails both import-propagation cases EXIT=1, and the mutation (negative control, restoring the swallow) fails test_facility_import_error_propagates[_find_compute_location] EXIT=1 while the resolve_location parametrization still passes because that path keeps its own guard. The head arm passes all 12. So a future re-widening of the facility-import catch reddens the suite rather than passing silently, and the unknown-facility fallback is covered by a real-config test. The change also raises with exc.add_note so the location flows into the traceback context, which is the diagnosability the plan asked for.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced every arm independently in scratch trees under $TMPDIR exported from git archive, each with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-codex/.venv and PYTHONPATH at the arm root: head (66aab5da) focused run '12 passed' EXIT=0, module.__file__ resolving to .../repro/head/imas_codex/remote/locations.py; the mutation (restore 'except Exception: return None' around the facility import in _find_compute_location) '1 failed, 1 passed' EXIT=1 with test_facility_import_error_propagates[_find_compute_location] failing; and the base arm (fd63244ce production with the head-authored test copied in) '2 failed' EXIT=1, both parametrizations failing, which is the recorded defect reproducing. These match the reviewed run's focused-head.log (12 passed), negative-control.log (1 failed, 1 passed) and pre-repair-refusal.log (2 failed). I also read the two default-marker gate logs directly: baseline-default-markers.log and head-default-markers.log each end '1 failed, 2096 passed' and '1 failed, 2101 passed' with the identical FAILED id tests/graph/test_cypher_property_check.py::test_repository_cypher_literals_have_declared_properties, so after-minus-baseline is 0 added failures. The shortfall in the record is focused-head.log's revision header naming fd63244ce for the head-tree run, which is what keeps this below the top band.
justifications.fit: the added symbols and tests are named by mechanism (test_facility_import_error_propagates, test_unknown_facility_keeps_direct_location_fallback) with no plan labels, section numbers or ticket ids in source; the docstrings state the behaviour they pin. The exception notes describe the mechanism ('while resolving location ...') rather than any tracker entry. No naming or fit defect.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's deliverable is wholly present: the three named handlers are narrowed to the condition each legitimately expects (import failure propagates; unknown facility = ValueError keeps the fallback; any other read error propagates with a location-naming note), and the two done-when behaviours are pinned by tests. The unknown-facility catch uses exactly the ValueError get_facility raises, which I confirmed at facility.py:139-140, so the narrowing is correct rather than merely plausible. The shortfall keeping this below the top is that the plan names the two error classes and requires the note to name the location being resolved, and the note text 'while resolving location {name!r}' names the compute-location search key in _find_compute_location rather than the original caller's location string (resolve_location passes its own location, so the caller-visible note is correct; the inner note is the search name). Minor and honest, not a defect.
justifications.reuse: the node reuses the existing resolve_location/_find_compute_location structure and the existing get_facility/list_facilities API rather than introducing parallel resolvers, and adds no new dependency. A small reuse note: the three narrowed handlers repeat the same 'except <Type> as exc: exc.add_note(f"while resolving location {...!r}"); raise' shape three times, and a shared helper would remove the repetition; but each site names a different variable and the repetition is three lines, so this is a note rather than a finding.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two commits touch only the three declared paths; no production file beyond locations.py, no dependency or lock change, no unrelated edit. The one blemish is the declared figures directory in orientation_write_paths that was not produced: the fragment (66aab5da's evidence) was written, so the node's evidence is complete, but the declaration and the deliverable disagree. That is a declared-but-not-produced shortfall rather than scope creep, which is why this sits at 16 rather than higher.
